decisions.reason: The same message's source-selection and production-scope changes are already fully represented by the candidate's existing message-179 MODIFY; the duration change requires no additional edit.
The candidate already has a complete message-179 MODIFY for standalone complete moments and the new production contexts; changing clip duration adds no further state change.
Message 179 requires complete lessons, stories, or real points but does not necessarily extend or alter the separate requirement to select strong or impactful moments.
The duration and output-platform decision says nothing about caption color, font, effects, or the scope of those visual-style rules.
Message 179 does not mention clean editing, effects, or transitions, so extending those trial-specific standards to monthly production would require inference.
The message reiterates personal approval and quota counting rules already present in the candidate state; the clip-duration modification does not alter the approval gate.
The candidate already records the message-179 daily cadence, while the 100-approved-clips rule was already current; the duration change does not require another quota MODIFY.
The source message does not change Lead Clipper responsibilities, advancement conditions, assignment status, or training focus.
The monthly 45–60 second production rule does not modify the already completed task-local qualification method or its recorded criteria.
The source decision does not address the channel or content used to submit sample clips for review.

Creating clips for Reels, Shorts, and TikTok does not necessarily assign publishing responsibility on all three platforms; the message still references an assigned Instagram account and does not replace the existing publishing destination.
